source: INFLUENCE's marks on the test bench (runs req-2yrn7wzs, set80, curated30, req-300qcqgo for techtiff.ai and divy.kairoth; 2026-10-13: req-xfj9GnAT, req-70Et4tKo and req-audience for imanoubou, danyel.design, photo_tvoritel and techburner). Each example paraphrases a marked Reel; post ids are kept for traceability. Sent to Jev inside the collaboration question.
rules: A Reel built around ONE named product, website, app, tool, restaurant or shop is a brand deal when it pushes the viewer towards it: a link or website in the caption, an @tag of the business account, 'comment X for access/the link', 'DM me for the name', a discount or price pitch, or a step-by-step demo of that one product.
News or an explainer about a big platform's own launch or feature (for example a new ChatGPT or Meta feature) is NOT a deal when there is no link, code, tag or call to action for it.
A list or roundup of several tools or places ('top 10 free tools', '3 websites') is NOT a deal unless one of them is singled out with its own call to action.
Credits to people ('co-creation credit @name', 'video credit @name', 'acting credit @name') are people, not brands.
The creator's own product, course or community is not a deal with a separate brand.

The word the viewer is asked to comment ('Comment TEAM', 'Comment STORM', 'Comment SCRIPT') is a code word, not the brand: the brand is the app, tool or product the Reel demonstrates or links to (Claude, CapCut, HeyGen).
Unboxing or showing off one new product while tagging its maker (@apple) is a deal with that maker.
Recommending what to buy in a named retailer's sale (Flipkart Big Billion Days) is a deal; the brand is the maker when one maker's products are pushed (Asus, Samsung), otherwise the retailer.
